claims: The Artemis II mission did not land on the moon.
The crew of the Artemis II mission completed a 10-day flyby mission around the moon.
The crew of the Artemis II mission safely returned to Earth.
The Orion spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission was designed to test life-support, navigation, and propulsion systems in deep space rather than to perform a lunar landing.
The crew of the Artemis II mission consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The four astronauts of the Artemis II mission were safely extracted by U.S. Navy helicopters approximately two hours after splashdown.
NASA is planning to land humans on the lunar surface during the Artemis III mission.
The Artemis III mission is currently slated for the coming years.
Projections for the Artemis III mission are as early as 2027–2028
